# Reform UK 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and implementing offshore processing for asylum seekers arriving illegally. Foreign criminals would face immediate deportation after serving sentences. A 20% National Insurance rate would apply to foreign workers (exempting healthcare workers and small businesses), with proceeds funding apprenticeships. Student visa rules would bar dependents, and a five-year residency requirement would apply before accessing benefits.

## Economic Policy
**Personal taxation:** Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 (removing 7 million people from income tax), cut stamp duty (0% below £750k), abolish inheritance tax for estates under £2 million, and reduce fuel duty by 20p per litre while scrapping VAT on energy bills.

**Business:** Exempt businesses with profits under £100,000 from corporation tax, reduce the main rate to 15% by year three, raise the VAT threshold to £150,000, abolish business rates for high street SMEs, and introduce a 4% online delivery tax for large multinationals.

## Public Spending
Proposed savings include stopping Bank of England interest payments on QE reserves (£35 billion annually), requiring 5% efficiency savings across departments, halving foreign aid, and improving tax collection.

## NHS
Proposals include tax exemptions for frontline staff, 20% tax relief on private healthcare, removing student loan debt for medical staff serving 10 years in the NHS, and introducing patient vouchers for private treatment when NHS waiting time targets are missed. Weekend operating theatre use would be mandated.

## Energy
The party would scrap Net Zero targets and renewable energy subsidies, fast-track North Sea oil and gas licensing, grant shale gas test licences, and develop small modular nuclear reactors.

## Law and Order
Plans include recruiting 40,000 new police officers, implementing zero-tolerance policing with increased stop-and-search powers, building 10,000 new detention places, and introducing mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders.

## Education
Proposals include curriculum changes requiring balanced teaching of historical topics, banning gender transitioning discussions in schools, providing 20% tax relief on private school fees, scrapping student loan interest, and restricting undergraduate numbers.

## Benefits
The party would enforce a "two-strike rule" requiring benefit claimants to accept employment within four months or after two job offers, with face-to-face assessments for disability benefits.

## Defence
Spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years, with a pay review for armed forces personnel and a dedicated veterans ministry.

## Housing
Proposals include fast-tracking brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, scrapping Section 24 tax rules for landlords, and abolishing the Renters' Reform Bill.

## Constitutional Changes
The party proposes leaving the ECHR, reforming the House of Lords, restricting postal voting, and holding a referendum on proportional representation.

## Brexit
Plans include rescinding remaining EU regulations, abandoning the Windsor Framework, and renegotiating the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

## Funding
Total annual savings claimed: £150 billion (including £50 billion from departmental efficiency, £35 billion from QE reserve interest, £30 billion from scrapping Net Zero). Additional growth assumptions project £10 billion in extra tax revenue. Total annual costs: £141 billion.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economic Policy
The manifesto proposes cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027 and abolishing self-employed National Insurance entirely. The "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure state pensions and pensioner tax allowances rise with inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit thresholds would shift to household income, starting withdrawal at £120,000 combined income.

## Taxation and Spending
The party commits to no increases in income tax, VAT, or Capital Gains Tax. Public sector net debt must fall, with borrowing below 3% of GDP. Defence spending would reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030. The civil service would return to pre-pandemic size, with reduced spending on consultants and diversity initiatives.

## Immigration
A legal cap on migration would be introduced, with annual parliamentary votes. The Rwanda removal scheme would operate monthly flights. Visa fees would increase, and health checks would be required for migrants. Asylum claims would be processed within six months.

## Housing
The target is 1.6 million homes in England, focusing on brownfield development. First-time buyers would pay no Stamp Duty on homes up to £425,000. A new Help to Buy scheme would offer 20% equity loans. Leasehold reforms would cap ground rents at £250.

## Healthcare
NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, recruiting 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors. Pharmacy First would expand, with 250 GP surgeries built or modernised. Social care costs would be capped from October 2025.

## Education and Youth
Mandatory National Service would offer military or civic service options for 18-year-olds. The Advanced British Standard would replace A-Levels and T-Levels. Mobile phones would be banned during school hours. 100,000 additional apprenticeships would be funded by closing underperforming university courses.

## Energy and Environment
Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds would continue. Offshore wind capacity would treble. Two Small Modular Reactor fleets would be approved. No new green levies would be introduced, and the £2 bus fare cap would continue throughout the parliament.

## Transport
£36 billion from HS2 savings would fund local transport, including £8.3 billion for road repairs. Great British Railways would be established. Road pricing would be banned, and London's ULEZ expansion reversed.

## Welfare Reform
Disability benefit assessments would be reformed, with mental health support potentially replacing cash payments. Benefit claims would close after 12 months if suitable jobs are refused. Fraud measures would receive enhanced powers.

## Devolution
The UK internal market would be protected. Funding would continue directly to Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland communities. The Windsor Framework commitments would be implemented for Northern Ireland.
